tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Urbanisation and Megacities

questions.question: Define the term urbanisation. (2 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Urbanisation is the increase in the proportion of a country's population living in urban areas (towns and cities) rather than rural areas (1 mark). It is caused by rural-urban migration (people moving from countryside to city) and natural increase (births exceeding deaths within urban populations) (1 mark).

questions.question: Explain how push and pull factors contribute to rural-urban migration. (4 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Push factors drive people away from rural areas - low agricultural wages, lack of services (healthcare, education, electricity), drought and famine, and lack of employment opportunities (1 mark). For example, in many LICs, rural farmers earn less than $2 per day, pushing them to seek better incomes in cities (1 mark). questions.question: Why are most megacities now located in LICs and NEEs? (6 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Most megacities are now in LICs and NEEs because these countries are experiencing the most rapid urbanisation (1 mark). HICs are already highly urbanised (over 75%) and their urban growth has slowed, meaning their cities grow slowly if at all (1 mark).
